record.publishedIn: Boissier P. E. & Reuter, G.F. 1852: Pugill. Pl. Afr. Bor. Hispan.

descriptions.description: "Plant 6-20(-30) cm, usually perennial, globose or elliptical, with a dense covering of stellate hairs, 0.8-1.5 mm in diameter, that completely obscure the epidermis of the stems, leaves and involucral bracts. Lacking glandular hairs. Stems 3-3.5 mm in diameter at the base, erect or ascending, branched from the base or in the upper half, with numerous leaves that are close to each other, giving a dense form. Basal leaves (0.6-)1.2-4.5 x (-0.2)0.6-1 cm, elliptic or linear-elliptic, with the petiole short and little differentiated; stem leaves 1-3.5 x 0.5-2 cm, sessile, cordiform. Capitula pedunculate or subsessile in the leaf axils, united in very dense racemose synflorescences on each branch. Involucre 6-7 x 5-7 mm, subcylindrical at flowering, stellate or with the bracts reflexed after dispersal, with two series of internal bracts and three supplementary bracts at the base of the involucre; internal bracts lanceolate, acute at apex, the outermost involute and each enclosing a flower or achene, the inner bracts flat and not enclosing a flower or achene. Receptacle alveolate, with lax hairs 0.8-1.5 mm. Flowers golden yellow, the outermost with the outer side or apex purplish. Anthers 2.2-2.5 mm, yellow. Stylar arms 0.2-0.3 mm, yellow. Achenes homomorphic, 1-1.3 x (0.35-)0.4-0.5 mm, the outermost somewhat larger than the inner, all with a pappus; pappus 4-4.5 mm, subplumose in the lower half, scabrous above, white, fragile."

The circumscription of Andryala arenaria follows Ferreira & al. (2019). These authors formally recognize three varieties: Plants with sinuate-dentate lower leaves densely covered with stellate trichomes and a dense racemiform synflorescence are recognised as var. ficalhoana, which is considered synonymous with A. cintrana and is restricted to coastal central Portugal. The other two varieties have lower leaves only moderately covered with stellate trichomes and a corymbiform synflorescence; of these var. pinnatifida has pinnatifid to pinnatisect lower leaves and occurs in NW Africa and Libya; the typical variety with subentire to sinuate-denate lower leaves occurs in the Iberian Peninsula and NW Africa (Morocco to Tunisia).
